draft.briefing: Hey, you're on Valiyaparamba, the longest island in Kerala! It's cut off from the mainland by the Kavvayi Backwater, fed by four rivers and dotted with little islands.
draft.hungryLine: Valiyaparamba is a fishing centre, so fresh fish is the move. Malabar-style meat and fish dishes are the local favourites.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Explore Edayilakkad, a marshy island in the Kavvayi Backwaters known for its biodiversity.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot by the Kavvayi Backwater and watch the fishing boats.
moodReplies.surprise-me: A National Waterway passes right through the island.

spots.name: Edayilakkad
spots.detail: In Valiyaparamba Panchayath · Marshy island rich in wildlife

spots.name: Bekal Fort
spots.detail: About 30 km · Fort on a headland into the sea

legends.title: Theyyam for Bhadrakali
legends.body: At Madiyan Koolam near Kanhangad, the temple is dedicated to Bhadrakali. During its festival, the ritual theyyam is performed.

legends.title: Open to everyone
legends.body: Ananda Ashramam in Kanhangad keeps a tradition of free food and lodging for all visitors. Its Panchavati Garden sits under five big trees.

tips.title: Cross by the bridge.
tips.body: The island is reached by crossing the Mavila Kadappuram bridge.

tips.title: Plan around theyyam season.
tips.body: Madiyan Koolam's theyyam festival falls in May/June and December/January.

story.title: An island of four rivers
story.body: Valiyaparamba is fed by four rivers and separated from the mainland by the Kavvayi Backwater.

story.title: A fishing island
story.body: About 11,917 people lived on the island, a noted fishing centre of the district.

story.title: Growing slowly
story.body: It's now one of the fastest-growing tourist spots in Kerala, with 13 wards and a National Waterway running through it.
